guideline.name: NICE NG125 — Surgical site infections: prevention and treatment
guideline.section: 1.3 Antibiotic prophylaxis before clean surgery involving a prosthesis or implant, clean-contaminated and contaminated surgery; single dose IV on starting anaesthesia; do not use routinely for clean non-prosthetic uncomplicated surgery; take allergy and local resistance into account. 1.4 SSI treatment: antibiotic covering likely organisms, local resistance and culture results
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Surgical site infections: prevention and treatment (NG125). London: NICE; 2019 (updated 2020).

guideline.name: SIGN 104 — Antibiotic prophylaxis in surgery
guideline.section: Procedure table: laparoscopic cholecystectomy — prophylaxis not recommended in low-risk patients (consider in high risk); open inguinal/femoral hernia repair with mesh — recommended/consider; colorectal surgery — highly recommended; a single dose is sufficient for most procedures; no evidence for post-operative doses
guideline.citation: Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network. Antibiotic prophylaxis in surgery (SIGN 104). Edinburgh: SIGN; 2008, updated 2014.

guideline.name: ASHP/IDSA/SIS/SHEA clinical practice guidelines for antimicrobial prophylaxis in surgery
guideline.section: Timing: within 60 minutes before incision; duration: single dose or < 24 h; beta-lactam allergy alternatives (colorectal: e.g. clindamycin or metronidazole with an aminoglycoside, aztreonam or a fluoroquinolone)
guideline.citation: Bratzler DW, Dellinger EP, Olsen KM, et al. Am J Health Syst Pharm. 2013;70:195–283.

guideline.name: NICE NG45 — Routine preoperative tests for elective surgery
guideline.section: Tables by surgical grade and ASA grade: ASA 1 minor/intermediate surgery — no routine FBC, U&E, ECG or haemostasis tests; do not routinely offer haemostasis tests (consider only for ASA 3–4 with chronic liver disease or when anticoagulant management needs it); ask women of childbearing potential about possible pregnancy and offer a test with consent
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Routine preoperative tests for elective surgery (NG45). London: NICE; 2016.

rationale: Permutation: clean surgery with a prosthesis where a single prophylactic dose is indicated and a post-operative course is not; also checks NICE NG45 test minimisation.
